F1.locus: abstract page header (submission line, title, authors)
F1.quote: [Submitted on 6 Apr 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 24 Sep 2026 (this version, v2)] … Title: Attribution Bias in Large Language Models … Authors: Eliza Berman , Bella Chang , Daniel B. Neill , Emily Black
F1.claim: the paper that introduces it, 'Attribution Bias in Large Language Models', by Eliza Berman, Bella Chang, Daniel B. Neill and Emily Black, submitted 6 April 2026, revised 24 September 2026
F1.checked_against: saved text B1.txt (sha256 cb64bc8db8a8755e…), whitespace-normalised; multi-part, each part checked

F2.quote: As Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used to support search and information retrieval, it is critical that they accurately attribute content to its original authors.
F2.claim: the motivation: LLMs used for search and retrieval must attribute content accurately to its original authors

F3.quote: In this work, we introduce AttriBench, the first fame- and demographically-balanced quote attribution benchmark dataset.
F3.claim: what it is: the first fame- and demographically-balanced quote attribution benchmark dataset
F3.lineage: what it is: a quote attribution benchmark

F4.quote: By explicitly balancing author fame and demographics, AttriBench enables controlled investigation of demographic bias in quote attribution.
F4.claim: its function: balancing author fame and demographics enables controlled investigation of demographic bias in quote attribution
F4.lineage: what it is: a quote attribution benchmark

F5.quote: Using this dataset, we evaluate 11 widely used LLMs across different prompt settings and find that quote attribution remains a challenging task even for frontier models.
F5.claim: finding: 11 widely used LLMs evaluated across prompt settings; quote attribution remains challenging even for frontier models

F6.quote: We observe large and systematic disparities in attribution accuracy between race, gender, and intersectional groups.
F6.claim: finding: large and systematic disparities in attribution accuracy between race, gender and intersectional groups

F7.quote: We further introduce and investigate suppression, a distinct failure mode in which models omit attribution entirely, even when the model has access to authorship information.
F7.claim: suppression defined: a distinct failure mode in which models omit attribution entirely though they have access to authorship information
F7.lineage: suppression: attribution omitted where authorship is available

F8.quote: We find that suppression is widespread and unevenly distributed across demographic groups, revealing systematic biases not captured by standard accuracy metrics.
F8.claim: finding: suppression is widespread and unevenly distributed across demographic groups, biases standard accuracy metrics do not capture
F8.lineage: suppression: attribution omitted where authorship is available

F9.quote: Our results position quote attribution as a benchmark for representational fairness in LLMs.
F9.claim: the authors' reading: quote attribution as a benchmark for representational fairness in LLMs
